title: Crispy Sun-Dried Tomato Turkey Burgers
changes_from_base: Turkey mince is kept juicy with Monterey Jack, wholemeal panko and yoghurt, flavoured with sun-dried tomato and basil, and pan-fried gently until the cheese crisps at the edges; topped with tomato and rocket.
summary: Sun-dried tomato and Monterey Jack studded turkey burgers stay moist within a golden crust, topped with peppery rocket and fresh tomato.

ingredients.item: turkey mince (about 7% fat, not extra-lean breast)
sun-dried tomatoes in oil, rinsed, patted dry and roughly chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine 450 g turkey mince, 50 g wholemeal panko breadcrumbs, 55 g grated Monterey Jack, 70 g chopped sun-dried tomatoes, 60 g plain low-fat yoghurt, 10 g chopped basil, ½ tsp fine salt and ½ tsp ground black pepper in a large bowl. Knead gently with your hands until just combined, being careful not to overwork the mixture.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Pat the mixture into 4 patties, each roughly 2 cm thick and 10 cm across. Season the outside of each patty lightly.

steps.title: Cook first side
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp rapeseed oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat until it shimmers, then add the patties. Cook without moving them for 5-7 minutes until the undersides are well browned.

steps.title: Cook second side
steps.text: Turn each patty and continue cooking for 6-9 minutes more, turning occasionally, until the second side is browned and the thickest part reaches 74 °C when checked with a thermometer.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Split and lightly toast 4 wholemeal burger buns and fill each with a warm patty.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top with sliced fresh tomato, 55 g baby rocket and a dollop of garlic mayonnaise if you like. Serve at once.

tips: Chop the sun-dried tomatoes finely so their sweet, tangy flavour spreads evenly through the turkey and no large pieces make the patties break apart.
Don't skip the gentle kneading step; it binds the mixture just enough to hold together while cooking, but overworking it will make the patties tough and dense.
Cook over a medium-low heat so the outside browns properly while the inside cooks through without burning.
Toast the buns lightly before assembling so they're warm and slightly crisp, giving a nice contrast to the tender burger.
storage: Best served and eaten straight away while the patties are still warm inside. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
